clue.text: Study journey in outline

parts.note: to con is an old verb meaning to study or learn by heart
a tour is a journey

explanation.surface: Someone plans to study a journey in outline before setting off.
explanation.definitionFit: The shape of a coastline or hill drawn as a line is its outline, the synonym here.

clue.text: Character actors

definitions.meaning: a ... of mind or features is its character or type
the actors in a play make up its company

explanation.definitionFit: The performers in a show together form it, and one's mould or type is another sense.

clue.text: Molluscs rest in middle of bed at sea

indicators.note: at sea means confused, so the letters are muddled into a new order

parts.note: anagram fodder

indicators.note: middle of picks the central letter of bed

explanation.surface: Shellfish resting in the middle of a seabed.
explanation.definitionFit: Nerites are a family of small sea snails, so they are molluscs.

clue.text: Abnormal fury when silver has been stolen

indicators.note: silver has been stolen means its symbol is taken away from the word

parts.note: outrage is fury
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: A victim's fury after the family silver is burgled.
explanation.definitionFit: A French borrowing meaning eccentric or unconventional, beyond the normal.

clue.text: Annals about monarch full of substance

indicators.note: the pair of words are full of the substance, which sits inside them

parts.note: re means about or concerning
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen
the gist is the substance or essence

explanation.surface: Historical records about a queen packed with real content.
explanation.definitionFit: An official list or record of events, like annals or a roll.

clue.text: Bit I added into total amount in bowl?

indicators.note: the bit and the I are added into the middle of the total amount, so they go inside it

parts.note: a sum is a total amount
a tad is a little bit
taken as written

explanation.surface: A bit of arithmetic: adding something into a running total.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the definition as an example: a sports arena is sometimes called a bowl.
explanation.definitionFit: A large sports arena is often called a bowl, as with American football venues, so the question mark flags an example.

clue.text: It's just stupid when politician kicks out one of the Liberals

indicators.note: the politician kicks out the letter and takes its place in the word

parts.note: silly means stupid
silly has two Ls; L is the abbreviation for Liberal, and one is removed
MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A complaint that it is foolish when an MP throws a Liberal out of the party.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb meaning merely or only, as in 'it was just a joke'.

clue.text: Fellow with diamonds in a row —- it's another precious stone

indicators.note: the fellow and diamonds go in the row, inside it

parts.note: a line is a row
a man is a fellow
D is the card abbreviation for diamonds

explanation.surface: A man with a row of diamonds is told it is a different gem.
explanation.definitionFit: A deep red variety of garnet, so a precious stone.

clue.text: One part of the Bible that has listeners crying

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
NT is the New Testament
ears are what we listen with

explanation.surface: A Bible reading that moves its audience to weep.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in this state is weeping, an idiomatic phrase for crying.

clue.text: Look down on the world from here and seem posher somehow

definitions.text: Look down on the world from here

indicators.note: somehow signals that the two words are rearranged in some unspecified way

parts.note: anagram fodder
anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Looking down on everyone from up there makes you seem grander.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Look down on' suggests snobbery, which the 'posher' surface supports; literally it is a high atmospheric layer.
explanation.definitionFit: A layer of the atmosphere about 50 to 85 km up, from which one would look down on Earth.

clue.text: Layers of rock with precious stone? That could be a trick

parts.note: strata are layers of rock
a gem is a precious stone

explanation.surface: A geologist's find of rock layers with a jewel inside might be a hoax.
explanation.definitionFit: A ruse or scheme to deceive is a synonym phrase for a trick.

clue.text: I'm turning over educational publication for little children

indicators.note: turning over means the letters of I'm are read backwards

parts.note: I'm without its apostrophe gives two letters
TES is the Times Educational Supplement, a British teachers' paper

explanation.surface: Someone flicks through a teachers' paper looking for something about small kids.
explanation.definitionFit: Small children are informally called mites, a fond word for tiny creatures.

clue.text: Satan and holiness clashing in two biblical books

indicators.note: the two words clashing are jumbled together into a new order

parts.note: anagram fodder
anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Evil and saintliness fighting each other in scripture.
explanation.definitionFit: The New Testament has First and Second epistles to the church at Thessalonica, two books.

clue.text: Abrasive old comedian getting tired in the auditorium

parts.note: Dick Emery was a British TV comedian of the 1960s and 70s

indicators.note: an auditorium is where things are heard, so the word for tired is said aloud

parts.note: bored means weary or tired

explanation.surface: A veteran comic's act grates while the theatre audience grows weary.
explanation.definitionFit: A nail file coated in grit, an abrasive strip for shaping nails.

clue.text: Port —- for some in Iberia the wine

parts.note: Muscat is the port and capital of Oman
el is the Spanish word for the, so for some people in Iberia

explanation.surface: Port, or something similar drunk in Spain or Portugal: which wine to order?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Port' looks like the drink, which suits the wine surface, but it is the Omani harbour city.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweet wine made from muscat grapes, so it is a named type of wine.

clue.text: Silly person securing new job — wouldn' she speak to anyone?

indicators.note: the silly person securing the rest holds it inside

parts.note: an ass is a fool
a chore is a job

explanation.surface: A foolish person landing a new job turns silent and aloof.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a cryptic hint: a female religious recluse withdraws from the world and speaks to no one.
explanation.definitionFit: A female religious hermit lives walled away from society, so she talks to nobody.

clue.text: Risk getting squiffy with companion supplying brandy

indicators.note: squiffy means drunk, so the word risk is reeling into a new order

parts.note: CH is Companion of Honour, a British order

explanation.surface: A drinking companion risks getting tipsy by handing round the brandy.
explanation.definitionFit: A clear fruit brandy distilled from cherries, so a specific kind of the spirit.

clue.text: Column finally given external support

indicators.note: the support is external, wrapping round the other word

parts.note: a pier is a supporting pillar
last means finally, as in 'last, we arrived'

explanation.surface: A pillar finally gets propping up from outside.
explanation.definitionFit: A rectangular column projecting from a wall, a decorative pillar.

clue.text: Fanciful decoration in yellow around clown

indicators.note: around here turns the word for yellow back to front

parts.note: or is the heraldic word for gold or yellow
Coco was a famous circus clown

explanation.surface: A clown dressed in yellow with flamboyant ornament.
explanation.definitionFit: An ornate eighteenth-century style of decoration full of scrolls and flourishes.

clue.text: A learner in cold Oxford college ultimately denied a bit of heat

indicators.note: the A and learner go in the other letters, inside them

parts.note: C is cold on a tap

indicators.note: the college is denied its ultimate, its last letter

parts.note: Oriel is an Oxford college
L is a learner driver

explanation.surface: A student in a chilly Oxford college is refused any warmth.
explanation.definitionFit: A unit of heat energy, so a small amount of heat.

clue.text: High-quality match — there's endless vitality about it

indicators.note: the shortened word for vitality sits about the match, holding it inside
endless means the word for vitality loses its final letter

parts.note: fire is spirit or vitality
a vesta is an old word for a wax match

explanation.surface: A top-class sports match full of energy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Match' looks like a sporting contest, but it is the wax kind you strike, an old-fashioned name. 'endless' trims the last letter before the wrap.
explanation.definitionFit: Hotels and restaurants rated with five stars are the best, so the term means top quality.

clue.text: Artist makes bond with traveller

parts.note: a tie is a bond
Marco Polo was the famous Venetian traveller

explanation.surface: A painter forms a link with a wanderer.
explanation.definitionFit: Giovanni Battista Tiepolo was an eighteenth-century Venetian painter.

clue.text: Bring down good drinks for all

parts.note: a round is drinks bought for everyone in a group

explanation.surface: Bring down some good drinks so everyone gets one.
explanation.definitionFit: To ground an aircraft or opponent is to force it down, the verb sense.

clue.text: I'll observe cat wandering around stately home

indicators.note: the letters of the fodder are wandering around into a new order

parts.note: anagram fodder, the apostrophe giving no letter
anagram fodder
anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A visitor watches a cat roaming the grounds of a country house.
explanation.walkthrough: BELVOIR CASTLE is a stately home in Leicestershire, England.
explanation.definitionFit: A grand historic castle in Leicestershire, the Duke of Rutland's seat, is an example of a stately home.

clue.text: Energy in a sort of jazz way of dancing

indicators.note: energy goes in the jazz word, inside it

parts.note: trad is traditional jazz
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Energetic movement in a jazz style of dance.
explanation.definitionFit: One's step or manner of walking, as in treading a measure, a dancer's step.

clue.text: Information on drug that affects someone's make-up

parts.note: gen is British slang for information
E is ecstasy

explanation.surface: Facts about a drug that alters a person's makeup.
explanation.definitionFit: A unit of heredity that determines a person's genetic constitution.

clue.text: Sort of nest in a country to the west

indicators.note: in an across clue, going to the west means reading right to left, backwards

parts.note: Eire is the Irish name for Ireland

explanation.surface: A bird's nest found in a country further west.
explanation.definitionFit: An eagle's lofty nest is called an eyrie, also spelt this way, so it is a type of nest.

clue.text: Maybe trying to repair telephone line is mad

definitions.text: Maybe trying to repair telephone line
definitions.meaning: an engineer fixing an overhead line literally climbs to the top of the post
British slang phrase meaning crazy or deluded

explanation.surface: Climbing about with a phone cable is a crazy business.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for crazy or mistaken; literally where a lineman perches to fix a phone line.

clue.text: Spoke to a daughter going out in finery?

indicators.note: the a and the daughter going out means they leave the longer word

parts.note: to address someone is to speak to them

explanation.surface: A father speaks to his daughter as she heads out for the evening in her best clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition has a question mark because being in finery is one way of being well clothed.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone wearing fine clothes is smartly attired, the adjective here.

clue.text: Communist took up arms showing an old battle emblem

parts.note: red is a common term for a communist
to rise is to take up arms in revolt, past tense rose

explanation.surface: A communist rebel took up arms under an old banner.
explanation.walkthrough: The red rose was the badge of the House of Lancaster in England's fifteenth-century Wars of the Roses.
explanation.definitionFit: The badge of Lancaster in the Wars of the Roses, a historic flower emblem of conflict.
